job-10:1:1.summary: Elijah asks the Lord to take his life; general weariness of life.

job-10:1:2.summary: Moses asks to be slain rather than see his misery; general despair.

job-10:1:3.summary: Jonah renounces his life; general despair, not bitter speech.

job-10:1:4.summary: Job says his life is being taken away; related despair but no weariness of soul shown.

job-10:1:5.summary: Eliphaz promises rescue in famine and war; no link to Job’s bitter speech.

job-10:1:6.summary: Eliphaz on the powerless escaping rulers; unrelated to Job’s complaint.

job-10:1:7.summary: Job asks to be heard and asks why he should not be angry; general resolve to speak.

job-10:1:8.summary: Silence wasted the psalmist until he confessed; loose contrast with Job letting words loose.

job-10:1:9.summary: Job asks God to grant his request to be ended; general despair.

job-10:1:10.summary: Job’s pains, worthless words and speaking under God’s arrows; same speaker’s anguish but no shared bitterness wording.

job-10:1:11.summary: “Leave me alone, for my life is empty”; Job’s same weariness of life.

job-10:1:12.summary: Life given to “those in bitterness” and “souls in pain” matches Job’s bitterness of soul.

job-10:1:13.summary: Jonah asks God to take his life; general despair.

job-10:1:14.summary: Hezekiah speaks of his “soul’s pain” taken away; brief verbal echo only.

job-10:1:15.summary: Later lines of the same speech describing God hunting Job; continuation rather than specific link.

job-10:1:16.summary: Speaking or silence brings no relief from wounds (truncated); related anguished speech.

job-10:1:17.summary: The Greek speaks of God choosing Hezekiah’s soul so it would not perish; no bitterness link in the text.

job-10:1:18.summary: Job refuses to be stopped by reproof; loosely matches letting his words loose.

job-10:1:19.summary: Job wishes to be hidden in Hades until wrath ceases; general despair.

job-10:1:20.summary: Job admits error lodges with him; no link to weariness or bitter speech.

job-10:2:0.summary: Psalmist asks God to test and show any lawlessness; loosely matches Job asking why he is judged.

job-10:2:1.summary: Job asks why he did not die if ungodly; related complaint, no shared plea.

job-10:2:2.summary: “Do not enter into judgment with Thy servant” parallels Job’s protest about being judged.

job-10:2:3.summary: Plea not to be rebuked in fury; general plea against divine discipline.

job-10:2:4.summary: Bildad urges supplication; general link to Job addressing the Lord.

job-10:2:5.summary: “No condemnation” echoes a Hebrew plea not to be condemned, which the Greek source rephrases.

job-10:2:6.summary: Examining one’s ways and confessing sin; general link only.

job-10:2:7.summary: Plea for mercy for God’s name’s sake; general plea.

job-10:2:8.summary: Plea not to be rebuked in fury, with suffering under God’s hand (truncated); general parallel.

job-10:2:9.summary: “Thou, show me; if I practiced injustice”; loose echo of asking God to explain judgment.

job-10:2:10.summary: Being judged by the Lord as discipline; general theme of divine judgment.

job-10:2:11.summary: Plea not to remember sins; general prayer, no specific link.

job-10:2:12.summary: Lament over sin and its consequences; general sorrow.

job-10:3:0.summary: “We are clay, all the work of Thy hands” echoes Job’s “works of Thy hands.”

job-10:3:1.summary: “Do not neglect the works of Thy hands” closely parallels Job’s complaint that God disowns them.
job-10:3:1.why: Appeal to God not to abandon His work.

job-10:3:2.summary: Job again pleads “Do not reject the works of Thy hands.”
job-10:3:2.why: Job’s recurring appeal as God’s creature.

job-10:3:3.summary: Jeremiah asks why the impious prosper, like Job’s charge that God favors the counsel of the ungodly.

job-10:3:4.summary: Elihu on insulting kings; no real link to the verse.

job-10:3:5.summary: Elihu says wrath rests on the ungodly; loose counterpoint to Job’s charge.

job-10:3:6.summary: God asks whether the one reproving Him will answer; loose response to Job’s charges.

job-10:3:7.summary: Elihu summarizes Job’s claim that the Lord removed his judgment; related to Job’s accusing question.

job-10:3:8.summary: Job says God “does not look upon the works of the ungodly,” loosely contrasting his charge here.
job-10:3:8.why: Job’s varying view of the wicked.

job-10:3:9.summary: Entrusting oneself to a faithful Creator in suffering; general link to God’s works.

job-10:3:10.summary: Job says wrath destroys great and ruler; general complaint of indiscriminate judgment.

job-10:3:11.summary: Elihu says God does not neglect the righteous; loose counterpoint.

job-10:3:12.summary: The Lord did not despise His bound ones; loose contrast with feeling disowned.
job-10:3:12.why: God does not reject the needy.

job-10:3:13.summary: Job says the earth is handed to an ungodly person’s hands with God behind it, the same charge of favoring the ungodly.
job-10:3:13.why: Job’s earlier version of the charge.

job-10:3:15.summary: God turns His hand against the sufferer (truncated); general lament of divine affliction.

job-10:3:16.summary: God says “Do not reject My judgment”; loosely answers Job’s accusing question.

job-10:3:17.summary: Bildad: the Lord will “not reject the innocent” nor accept the ungodly, directly opposing Job’s charge.

job-10:4:1.summary: God knows hearts, unlike human judgment; general contrast of divine and human sight.

job-10:4:2.summary: “Thou art not a human being like me”; same contrast between God and humans.
job-10:4:2.why: Job’s earlier statement of the same point.

job-10:4:3.summary: Christ’s eyes like flame; no real link to whether God sees as mortals do.

job-10:5:0.summary: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years; general contrast of God’s time with human time.

job-10:5:2.summary: “Thy years will not fail” contrasts God’s years with human years.

job-10:5:3.summary: “Thy years extend through a generation of generations” and “Thy years will not fail.”

job-10:5:4.summary: The number of God’s “years is also boundless,” answering whether God’s years are a man’s.

job-10:5:5.summary: The Lord remains for ever; general eternity theme.

job-10:6:0.summary: God numbers Job’s practices and lets no sin pass, like searching out his sins.
job-10:6:0.why: Job’s sense of God scrutinizing sin.

job-10:6:1.summary: The sinful man’s sin “will be sought out,” echoing God searching out sins.

job-10:6:2.summary: Blood found on Israel’s hands; no shared searching of sins in the Greek wording.

job-10:6:3.summary: God searches Jerusalem with a lamp to exact judgment, like searching out lawlessness.
job-10:6:3.why: Image of God searching out sin.

job-10:6:4.summary: “Will God not search these things out?” matches God searching out sins.

job-10:6:5.summary: The Lord will reveal hidden things of hearts; general divine scrutiny.

job-10:6:6.summary: Same speech: God watching Job’s lawlessness and “renewing my examination,” developing this complaint.

job-10:6:7.summary: Jesus knows what is within a person; general divine knowledge.

job-10:7:1.summary: The Lord affirms Job spoke truly, vindicating his claim of innocence.

job-10:7:2.summary: No one snatches from the Father’s hand; inverted echo of no rescue from God’s hands.
job-10:7:2.why: God’s hand as security, not threat.

job-10:7:3.summary: “What god will rescue you from my hands?” shares the phrase but in a tyrant’s mouth.

job-10:7:4.summary: God tests and knows the psalmist; general divine knowledge.

job-10:7:5.summary: Psalmist protests his innocence and asks God to test him, like Job’s appeal to God’s knowledge.

job-10:7:6.summary: “If there is injustice in my hands” – an oath-like protest of innocence like Job’s.

job-10:7:7.summary: Plea to be judged by one’s innocence before the God who tests hearts.

job-10:7:8.summary: “Thou knowest that I love Thee” shares the “Thou knowest that I” appeal in another setting.

job-10:7:9.summary: Who contradicts Him? Whatever He wishes He does; matches no rescue from God’s hands.

job-10:7:10.summary: Job asks what answer he could make if examined; general theme.

job-10:7:11.summary: “He already knows my way, and He tested me like gold”; Job appeals to God’s knowledge of his innocence.

job-10:7:12.summary: Plea to be tested for lawlessness; general innocence theme.

job-10:7:13.summary: “Lest He seize you and there be no rescuer” echoes no one to rescue from God’s hands.

job-10:7:14.summary: “The Lord knows my innocence” – Job’s same appeal to God’s knowledge.

job-10:7:15.summary: The Lord knows the way of the righteous; general theme.

job-10:7:16.summary: Job wishes for a hearing; general legal appeal.

job-10:7:17.summary: God as witness of blameless conduct; general appeal to God’s knowledge.

job-10:7:18.summary: “No one will deliver her from My hand” matches no rescue from God’s hands.
job-10:7:18.why: Same idea of inescapable divine hand.

job-10:7:19.summary: God tested the psalmist and “no injustice was found,” like Job’s claim God knows his innocence.

job-10:7:20.summary: A clear conscience before God; general innocence theme.

job-10:8:0.summary: “Thy hands made me and formed me” is nearly identical to Job’s words.
job-10:8:0.why: Same confession of God as Maker.

job-10:8:1.summary: Earlier in the speech Job calls himself “the works of Thy hands.”

job-10:8:2.summary: God “fashioned him, formed him, and made him,” echoing molding and making.

job-10:8:3.summary: The potter remakes or destroys the vessel he shaped (truncated), like God molding then striking Job.
job-10:8:3.why: Potter image of making and unmaking.

job-10:8:4.summary: God regrets making mankind and resolves to blot it out; loose parallel of Maker turning to destroy.

job-10:9:1.summary: “We are clay, all the work of Thy hands” matches Job molded as clay.

job-10:9:3.summary: Dust returns to the earth, as Job says God turns him back into earth.

job-10:9:4.summary: “Remember” plea for mercy; shared imperative only.

job-10:9:5.summary: “Like the potter’s clay in My hands” parallels being molded as clay.

job-10:9:6.summary: Potter’s clay questioning the potter, the same clay image.

job-10:9:7.summary: The potter’s authority over the clay, the same image.

job-10:9:8.summary: Brought down “into the dust of death,” like being turned back to earth.

job-10:9:9.summary: Calling decay his mother; general mortality theme.

job-10:9:10.summary: “Remember… that my life is a breath” – Job’s same appeal for God to recall his frailty.

job-10:9:11.summary: “Remember what my existence is” – appeal to God about human frailty and creation.

job-10:9:12.summary: Plea for God to see affliction; general plea.

job-10:9:13.summary: “Remember us, Lord”; shares the plea only.

job-10:9:14.summary: The Greek reads “Return, sons of men” without dust; the return-to-earth link is weakened.

job-10:10:0.summary: God forming the unformed substance in secret, describing formation in the womb.
job-10:10:0.why: God’s care in forming the embryo.

job-10:10:1.summary: “Taking form in blood” from seed over months, describing gestation like milk curdled.

job-10:11:0.summary: Sinews, flesh, skin and bones assembled, the same list as Job 10:11.

job-10:11:1.summary: Behemoth’s sinews “woven together”; verbal echo of being threaded together.

job-10:11:2.summary: The body held together by joints; loose image of knit frame.

job-10:11:3.summary: Longing to be clothed with a heavenly dwelling; only the clothing image is shared.

job-10:11:4.summary: The mother did not arrange the body’s composition in the womb; God formed it, as Job says.
job-10:11:4.why: God as former in the womb.

job-10:12:0.summary: In Him we live and move; general dependence for life.

job-10:12:1.summary: “Divine spirit is what made me,” paralleling God’s care guarding Job’s spirit and life.
job-10:12:1.why: God as source of spirit and life.

job-10:12:2.summary: God gives everyone life and breath; general source of life.

job-10:12:3.summary: Lot speaks of mercy and preserving life; shared words in a different setting.

job-10:12:4.summary: Do not be anxious about life; no specific link to God granting and guarding life.

job-10:13:0.summary: “Whatever He Himself wished, He also did” – God’s unhindered power.

job-10:13:1.summary: God kills and makes alive; general sovereignty.

job-10:13:2.summary: “I will do everything I have planned” – God’s counsel always accomplished.

job-10:13:3.summary: Things happen only as the Lord commands; general sovereignty.

job-10:13:4.summary: God acts unseen; loosely matches things hidden within God.

job-10:13:5.summary: God’s eternal purpose accomplished; general purpose theme.

job-10:13:6.summary: God’s unsearchable judgments; general hidden wisdom.

job-10:13:7.summary: God does all things, peace and calamity; general sovereignty.

job-10:13:8.summary: A God not known; loose link to things held within God.

job-10:13:9.summary: Humans do not know what will be; general limits of knowledge.

job-10:14:1.summary: If God closely watches lawless deeds, who withstands? Like God guarding Job when he sins.

job-10:14:2.summary: God tests and knows; general scrutiny.

job-10:14:3.summary: God takes away sin yet will “in no wise cleanse the guilty,” like not acquitting Job.
job-10:14:3.why: God does not acquit the guilty.

job-10:14:4.summary: “Thou wilt not leave me innocent” – Job’s same complaint of not being acquitted.

job-10:14:5.summary: God records Job’s sins and watches all his works.

job-10:14:6.summary: “Yet not cleansing the guilty” parallels God not acquitting lawlessness.

job-10:14:7.summary: God numbers Job’s practices; no sin passes Him.

job-10:15:0.summary: “Woe to the lawless” matches Job’s “if I am ungodly, alas for me.”

job-10:15:1.summary: “Even if I am righteous, He will not listen” – Job’s same dilemma.

job-10:15:3.summary: Job’s earlier claim of innocence in the same speech; loose link.

job-10:15:4.summary: Distinction between righteous and lawless; general theme.

job-10:15:5.summary: “Woe is me” in a confession of uncleanness; shared cry only.

job-10:15:6.summary: Plea for God to see humiliation; general link to Job’s dishonor.

job-10:15:7.summary: Sinners turn back to Hades; general fate of the ungodly.

job-10:15:8.summary: Overthrow of the ungodly; general fate of the wicked.

job-10:15:9.summary: Wrath upon evildoers; general woe on the ungodly.

job-10:15:10.summary: Unprofitable slaves even after doing all; loose humility theme.

job-10:15:11.summary: Job agitated and in pain; general distress.

job-10:15:12.summary: No one can question God; general helplessness.

job-10:15:13.summary: Communal lament of reproach and suffering (truncated); general parallel.

job-10:15:15.summary: “Since I am ungodly” – Job’s same conditional about being ungodly.

job-10:15:16.summary: Righteousness like a rag; loose link to righteousness bringing no honor.

job-10:15:17.summary: God seeing Israel’s affliction; the Greek source has no plea to see affliction.

job-10:15:18.summary: Job agitated before God; general distress.

job-10:15:19.summary: “See my humiliation” depends on Hebrew wording of Job 10:15 not present in the Greek text.

job-10:16:0.summary: A lion crushing bones; shares lion imagery but God is the lion, not the hunted.

job-10:16:2.summary: God’s extraordinary works; the Greek source says God destroys Job terribly, not marvelously.

job-10:16:3.summary: Extraordinary plagues; link depends on Hebrew wording not in the Greek source.

job-10:16:4.summary: A roaring lion; only lion imagery shared.

job-10:16:5.summary: God like a predator tearing; loose image of God destroying.

job-10:16:6.summary: Korah swallowed by the earth; no real link to the verse.

job-10:17:0.summary: God seizing Job and it becoming “a testimony”; loose link to renewed examination.

job-10:17:1.summary: The Lord afflicted Naomi; general divine affliction.

job-10:17:2.summary: God handing Job over and assaulting him repeatedly – the same complaint of God’s anger.

job-10:17:3.summary: Moab undisturbed like wine on lees; no link in the Greek.

job-10:17:4.summary: Those with “no exchange” do not fear God; incidental word only.

job-10:17:5.summary: God searching Jerusalem; loose link to examination.

job-10:17:6.summary: “He dealt with me terribly in anger” – Job’s same complaint of God’s great anger.

job-10:18:0.summary: “Why did I come out from the womb” – Jeremiah’s same lament over birth.

job-10:18:1.summary: A dead man is gone; general death theme.

job-10:18:3.summary: Better not to have been born; similar wish but different person.

job-10:18:4.summary: “Woe to me, mother! What sort of man did you give birth to” – lament over one’s birth.

job-10:18:5.summary: Eyes of the ungodly waste away; only the word “eye” shared.

job-10:19:0.summary: Taken away and “did not see the sun” loosely evokes a life that never began.

job-10:20:0.summary: A mortal is “short-lived,” matching Job’s “time of my life short.”

job-10:20:1.summary: “Give me relief… before I depart and no longer exist” parallels “let me rest a little” before going.

job-10:20:3.summary: Days made “handbreadths,” existence as nothing; brevity of life.

job-10:20:4.summary: “My life is swifter than a runner” – Job’s same lament of brevity.

job-10:20:5.summary: Days like grass; general brevity theme.

job-10:20:6.summary: Life on earth is a shadow (Bildad); general brevity.

job-10:20:7.summary: Job’s life is a breath and lighter than chatter; same lament of fleeting life.

job-10:20:8.summary: Plea for God to keep His hand away; loose link to plea for rest.

job-10:21:0.summary: “Darkness” and “gloom” shared with Job’s “dark and gloomy land.”

job-10:21:1.summary: The dead “will not return,” matching going where one will not return.

job-10:21:2.summary: “A way on which I will not return” – Job’s same phrase for death.

job-10:21:4.summary: A man who dies is gone and will not rise; finality of death, with Hades.

job-10:21:5.summary: Water poured out and not gathered; general irreversibility of death.

job-10:21:6.summary: Walking through death’s shadow; only darkness of death shared.

job-10:21:7.summary: Job imagines rest in death; general theme.

job-10:21:8.summary: The grave as “darkness” and a “forgotten land,” like the dark land of no return.

job-10:21:9.summary: “In dark places and in death’s shadow” – the same dark realm of the dead.

job-10:21:10.summary: A desolate land no one passed through; only a loose land image.

job-10:21:11.summary: Hezekiah will no longer see God or people; general departure.

job-10:22:1.summary: Covered by death’s shadow; general darkness of death.

job-10:22:2.summary: Gates of death and Hades; general underworld.

job-10:22:3.summary: Darkness and death’s shadow; general imagery.

job-10:22:4.summary: Israel’s wilderness journey; the desolate land is not the land of darkness.

job-10:22:5.summary: A fixed chasm no one crosses; loosely matches the realm of no return.

job-10:22:6.summary: Darkness and gloom taking possession – Job’s same imagery of darkness.

job-10:22:7.summary: Death’s shadow; only general darkness theme.

job-10:22:8.summary: No place for evildoers to hide; the Greek has no darkness link.

job-11:2:0.summary: Bildad tells Job to stop talking, like Zophar rebuking his many words.

job-11:2:1.summary: Slow to speak; general caution on words.

job-11:2:3.summary: Job dismisses “words of wind,” the same quarrel over empty speech.

job-11:2:4.summary: “How long will you speak these things?” – a friend’s same complaint about Job’s many words.

job-11:2:5.summary: Paul called a “babbler”; loose talker theme.

job-11:2:6.summary: “A talkative man will not be set straight,” matching rebuke of one who says much.

job-11:3:0.summary: Job weary pleads; no shared element in the Greek.

job-11:3:1.summary: Mockery and gnashing; the Greek source has no mocking.

job-11:3:2.summary: Shaming the disobedient; no shame or mockery in the Greek source.

job-11:3:3.summary: Last-days mockers; the Greek source lacks mocking.

job-11:3:4.summary: Job calls friends unjust physicians; general dispute.

job-11:3:5.summary: Job as object of mockery; the Greek source has no mockery.

job-11:3:6.summary: Who can reduce my words to nothing? Loosely about contending words.

job-11:3:7.summary: God examining the friends; no shared element.

job-11:3:8.summary: Opponent left with nothing to say; loose link to no one to contend.

job-11:3:9.summary: Job asks to speak without being laughed at; loose debate theme.

job-11:3:10.summary: Jeremiah sits alone apart from merrymakers; no link.

job-11:3:11.summary: Job “drinking mockery”; the Greek source lacks mockery.

job-11:3:12.summary: Eliphaz rebukes Job’s unprofitable speeches, like Zophar’s rebuke of lengthy talk.

job-11:3:13.summary: Faces filled with dishonor; no link in the Greek.

job-11:4:1.summary: Job claims he has not falsified God’s words; loose claim of integrity.

job-11:4:2.summary: How can a mortal be righteous before the Lord; general theme.

job-11:4:3.summary: Elihu reports Job saying “I am righteous,” the same claim Zophar quotes.

job-11:4:4.summary: “Who are you to say, ‘I am righteous before the Lord’?” – same rebuke of Job’s claim.

job-11:4:5.summary: No one clean from filth; general counterpoint to claiming purity.

job-11:4:6.summary: Giving a defense of hope; no link.

job-11:4:7.summary: Job asserts no injustice on his tongue, the kind of claim Zophar rejects.

job-11:4:8.summary: Job questions God about sin; loose link.

job-11:5:1.summary: Job longs to hear the words God would say to him, answering Zophar’s wish that God would speak.
job-11:5:1.why: Job’s desire for God to speak.

job-11:5:2.summary: When the Lord speaks, He rebukes the friends, not Job – reversing Zophar’s expectation.

job-11:5:3.summary: Job wishes for someone to hear him; general hearing theme.

job-11:5:4.summary: Elihu quotes Job and speaks for God (truncated); loose link.
job-11:5:4.why: Another voice claiming to speak for God.

job-11:5:5.summary: The Lord actually answers Job and Job falls silent, fulfilling the wish that God would speak.

job-11:5:6.summary: God’s question to Job; loose link to God speaking.

job-11:6:0.summary: Suffering because of evil deeds; general link to punishment fitting sins.

job-11:6:2.summary: God discloses mysteries; loose link to God telling wisdom.

job-11:6:3.summary: Parables of hidden things; no link in the Greek.

job-11:6:4.summary: Mystery revealed to apostles; no link.

job-11:6:5.summary: Has wisdom arrived at you? Loose wisdom-dispute link.

job-11:6:6.summary: Eliphaz says Job was scourged for few of his sins, like Zophar’s claim his suffering fits his sins.

job-11:6:7.summary: God reveals mysteries to Daniel; no link.

job-11:6:8.summary: God is wise and mighty; general wisdom.

job-11:6:10.summary: Hidden things belong to the Lord; general wisdom theme.

job-11:6:11.summary: God makes His covenant known; loose revelation theme.

job-11:6:12.summary: Job guilty through his words; general accusation.

job-11:6:13.summary: God has not repaid according to sins, contrasting Zophar’s claim that suffering is worthy of sins.

job-11:6:14.summary: God’s mercy despite sin; general theme.

job-11:6:15.summary: God reveals hidden things by the Spirit; general wisdom.

job-11:6:16.summary: God tells humans what wisdom is; loose link.

job-11:7:1.summary: “His greatness has no limit” – God beyond reach.

job-11:7:2.summary: Humans “may not find out the work God has done from beginning to end.”

job-11:7:3.summary: God fashioned earth’s extremities and “His understanding cannot be discovered.”

job-11:7:4.summary: “Untraceable riches”; shared idea of untraceable only.

job-11:7:6.summary: “Thy tracks will not be known” matches finding no trace of the Lord.

job-11:7:7.summary: “We do not find another like Him” – God beyond finding.

job-11:7:8.summary: We hear only “parts of His way” – God’s works beyond full grasp.

job-11:7:9.summary: No one knows the Father except by revelation; general knowledge theme.

job-11:7:10.summary: The Spirit searches the depths of God; general theme.

job-11:7:11.summary: Who has known the Lord’s mind; general theme.

job-11:7:12.summary: “Who has traced out the things in heaven?” matches finding a trace of the Lord.

job-11:7:13.summary: “Who can trace the height of heaven… the abyss”; same rhetorical question.

job-11:7:14.summary: “Impossible to trace out the Lord’s wonders.”

job-11:7:15.summary: Who can recount God as He is; general theme.

job-11:8:0.summary: God dwelling on high; general height theme.

job-11:8:2.summary: Heaven distant from earth as God’s ways; general height contrast.

job-11:8:3.summary: Hades and heaven as extremes God reaches, like heaven high and deeper than Hades.

job-11:8:4.summary: God’s praise over earth and heaven; general theme.

job-11:8:5.summary: “Hades is naked before Him” – God knows depths beyond human reach.

job-11:8:6.summary: How high the clouds are; general height.

job-11:8:7.summary: Heaven cannot contain God; general vastness.

job-11:8:8.summary: “Breadth and length and height and depth” surpassing knowledge, like Job 11:8–9’s dimensions.

job-11:8:9.summary: “Heaven is high and earth deep” – nearly the same phrase.

job-11:8:10.summary: Heaven’s height above earth as measure of mercy; general height image.

job-11:9:0.summary: Sea’s farthest reaches still within God’s hand; loose dimensions theme.

job-11:9:1.summary: God observes all and measures waters; general theme.

job-11:9:2.summary: God of earth’s ends and the sea; general vastness.

job-11:10:1.summary: “If He throws down, who will build?” – no one can reverse God’s overturning.

job-11:10:2.summary: He shuts and no one opens; general irresistible authority.

job-11:10:5.summary: Who resisted God and endured; general theme.

job-11:10:6.summary: Not enclosed in enemy hands; no link in the Greek.

job-11:10:7.summary: “He will provide quiet, and who will condemn?” – none can question God’s acts.

job-11:10:8.summary: God delivering Israel to enemies; no link.

job-11:10:9.summary: God fencing the sea; no link.

job-11:10:10.summary: God strikes and heals; general sovereignty.

job-11:11:0.summary: “Thou seest” trouble and acts on it, like God seeing improper things.

job-11:11:1.summary: All things laid open to His eyes; God overlooks nothing.

job-11:11:2.summary: God searches hearts and repays according to works.

job-11:11:3.summary: Jesus knows what is in people; general knowledge.

job-11:11:4.summary: Habakkuk asks why God looks on evil silently; loose contrast.

job-11:11:5.summary: “The Lord knows human reasonings, that they are futile” – God knows human vanity.

job-11:11:6.summary: God remembers all their evils; they are before His face.

job-11:11:7.summary: Claim that God cannot see through clouds, the opposite of Zophar’s claim.

job-11:11:8.summary: The Lord examines hearts to repay each by his ways.

job-11:11:9.summary: Officials watching over officials; loose oversight theme.

job-11:11:10.summary: The wicked say God turned away “so as never to see,” the opposite of Zophar’s point.

job-11:11:12.summary: “Thou hast seen, Lord”; general divine seeing.

job-11:12:0.summary: The wild donkey of the wilderness, the same animal image.

job-11:12:1.summary: “Empty man”; loose echo of vain person.

job-11:12:2.summary: Wilderness and wind-driven desire, but the Greek shown omits the donkey.

job-11:12:3.summary: True versus earthly wisdom; no specific link.

job-11:12:4.summary: “I became beastlike” – human folly compared to a beast.

job-11:12:5.summary: Humans shown to be beasts – humans compared to animals.

job-11:12:7.summary: By nature children of wrath; general human nature.

job-11:12:8.summary: Conceived in sin; loose link to “born of woman.”

job-11:12:9.summary: Job sarcastically answers that wisdom will die with the friends, rebutting Zophar’s jibe.

job-11:12:10.summary: Do not be wise in your own eyes; general theme.

job-11:12:11.summary: The senseless will not understand; general folly.

job-11:12:12.summary: Claiming wisdom, becoming fools; general theme.

job-11:12:13.summary: Sons of men are vain; general vanity.

job-11:12:14.summary: Worldly wisdom is folly; general theme.

job-11:12:15.summary: Job’s own “wild donkey” image, used in his complaint.

job-11:12:16.summary: God catches the wise; general wisdom theme.

job-11:12:17.summary: Confession of foolishness and God’s unknowable ways; general theme.

job-11:12:18.summary: True wisdom is reverence for God; general theme.

job-11:13:0.summary: “I spread out my hands unto Thee” matches turning hands upward in prayer.

job-11:13:1.summary: “I spread my hands toward Thee” – same prayer gesture.

job-11:13:2.summary: Prepare your hearts toward the Lord; general repentance.

job-11:13:3.summary: A generation that did not direct its heart; general theme.

job-11:13:4.summary: Bildad: seek God in supplication; “if you are pure,” He will restore you – same counsel.

job-11:13:5.summary: Slave who did not prepare; no link.

job-11:13:6.summary: Did not direct his heart to seek the Lord; general heart theme.

job-11:13:7.summary: Ethiopia hastens its hand toward God; loose gesture link.

job-11:13:8.summary: Eliphaz urges receiving God’s words; general repentance counsel.

job-11:13:9.summary: Eliphaz would entreat the Lord; general prayer counsel.

job-11:13:10.summary: Directed heart to seek the Lord; general theme.

job-11:14:0.summary: “You have put injustice far from your dwelling” – nearly the same wording.

job-11:14:1.summary: “Cleanse your hands… purify your hearts,” matching pure heart and putting lawlessness from hands.

job-11:14:2.summary: The pure do not perish; general retribution.

job-11:14:3.summary: Not adding to injustice; general repentance.

job-11:14:6.summary: “Cast away from yourselves all your impieties” – same call to remove lawlessness.

job-11:14:7.summary: A curse that will “lodge within his house”; shared word, different idea.

job-11:14:8.summary: Walking in innocence within my house; loose link.

job-11:15:0.summary: Eliphaz promises looking up cheerfully toward heaven, like a shining, unafraid face.

job-11:15:1.summary: Confidence without shame at His coming; general theme.

job-11:15:2.summary: Confidence toward God when heart does not condemn; general theme.

job-11:15:3.summary: Lifting holy hands; loose prayer-gesture link.

job-11:15:4.summary: Whom will I fear? General fearlessness.

job-11:15:5.summary: The righteous is confident; general theme.

job-11:15:6.summary: The righteous will not fear; general theme.

job-11:15:8.summary: Cain’s fallen face; loose contrast with a shining face.

job-11:15:9.summary: Not ashamed when looking on commandments; general theme.

job-11:15:10.summary: Hope of strength in the fear of the Lord; general theme.

job-11:15:11.summary: Job said he “cannot look up” full of dishonor; Zophar promises a shining face.

job-11:16:1.summary: Not remembering days due to gladness; general forgetting.

job-11:16:2.summary: Waters of Noah’s time passed; loose water image.

job-11:16:3.summary: The mother “no longer remembers the anguish,” like forgetting toil.

job-11:16:4.summary: “You will forget lasting shame” and “Do not fear,” matching forgetting toil without terror.

job-11:16:5.summary: Tears wiped away after tribulation; general comfort.

job-11:16:6.summary: “God has made me forget all my toil” – same idea and word.

job-11:16:7.summary: “I will not fear” after God’s wrath turns away; general theme.

job-11:16:8.summary: Water covering the sleeper; loose contrasting water image.

job-11:16:9.summary: “Forget their poverty and no longer remember their troubles.”

job-11:16:10.summary: “Like… a wave they passed me by” – the same passing-wave simile in Job.

job-11:16:11.summary: No more flood; loose water theme.

job-11:17:0.summary: Light rising early and darkness becoming “like noon,” matching life rising from noon.

job-11:17:2.summary: Ways of the righteous shine increasingly; general light theme.

job-11:17:3.summary: Light toward evening; loose light image.

job-11:17:4.summary: The Lord will bring me into light; general restoration.

job-11:17:5.summary: God found ready like dawn; general dawn image.

job-11:17:6.summary: Light sprang up in darkness for the upright; general theme.

job-11:17:7.summary: Job’s latter days are blessed more than the former (truncated), fulfilling the promised restoration.

job-11:17:8.summary: Flourishing in old age; general theme.

job-11:17:9.summary: David’s blessing of God; no link.

job-11:17:10.summary: A sun of righteousness will rise; general rising light.

job-11:17:11.summary: Simeon’s song of light for nations; no specific link.

job-11:18:0.summary: Fearless sleep and freedom from fright because the Lord supports you – security as promised.

job-11:18:1.summary: Lying down and waking with God’s help; general security.

job-11:18:2.summary: Hope in God amid grief; general hope theme.

job-11:18:3.summary: “In peace I will… sleep… in hope” – peace and hope together, as in the source.

job-11:18:4.summary: Dwelling securely and peace in the land; general blessing.

job-11:18:5.summary: Hope that does not shame; general hope theme.

job-11:18:6.summary: One trusting in piety is righteous; general confidence.

job-11:18:7.summary: Job said his life perished “in empty hope”; Zophar promises real hope.

job-11:18:8.summary: Eliphaz’s promise of restored righteousness and brightness; general parallel.

job-11:18:9.summary: Christ in you the hope of glory; only the word “hope” shared.

job-11:18:10.summary: Job asks what strength or time remains; loose contrast with promised hope.

job-11:19:0.summary: Former oppressors come to Zion in fear, loosely like many entreating the restored person in Job 11:19.
job-11:19:0.why: Shows reversal where adversaries seek out the favored one.

job-11:19:1.summary: Both promise freedom from war and from anyone who frightens, a secure quiet life under God’s blessing.
job-11:19:1.why: Ties Zophar’s promise to the covenant blessing of peace.

job-11:19:2.summary: Nations bow and pray to Israel, broadly like many entreating the restored person.
job-11:19:2.why: General image of others seeking out the blessed.

job-11:19:3.summary: The rich will “entreat your favor,” echoing the promise that many will “entreat you.”
job-11:19:3.why: Same image of others courting the favored one.

job-11:19:5.summary: Opponents are made to bow before the faithful church, a loose parallel to many entreating Job.

job-11:19:6.summary: “Many” attend the faces of kings, a general echo of many seeking the prosperous person’s favor.
job-11:19:6.why: Proverbial note on courting the powerful.

job-11:19:7.summary: Abimelech, once hostile, seeks peace and a covenant with blessed Isaac, illustrating others entreating the favored one; range truncated.
job-11:19:7.why: Narrative example of enemies seeking peace.

job-11:20:0.summary: “Failing eyes” and a wasting soul under curse parallel the eyes of the ungodly wasting away.
job-11:20:0.why: Links the wicked’s end to the covenant curses.

job-11:20:1.summary: Job says “my eyes wasted away,” sharing the idiom but applied to his own grief, not the ungodly.
job-11:20:1.why: Shows Job feeling the fate Zophar assigns the wicked.

job-11:20:2.summary: Job denies making a widow’s eye “waste away,” sharing only the wasting-eye idiom.
job-11:20:2.why: Same idiom of failing eyes in a different context.

job-11:20:3.summary: No escape for those neglecting salvation loosely echoes deliverance abandoning the wicked.

job-11:20:4.summary: Eyes fail from hoping in God, sharing the failing-eyes and hope motif but for the righteous sufferer.
job-11:20:4.why: Contrasts hopeful waiting with the wicked’s doomed hope.

job-11:20:5.summary: “Our eyes failed” looking vainly for help, echoing failing eyes and absent deliverance.
job-11:20:5.why: Similar picture of vain hope for rescue.

job-11:20:6.summary: The impious is swept into destruction, a general parallel to the ungodly whose hope is destruction.
job-11:20:6.why: Proverbial statement of the same outcome.

job-11:20:7.summary: No hiding place for lawdoers loosely parallels deliverance abandoning the wicked.
job-11:20:7.why: Same theme of no escape for evildoers.

job-11:20:9.summary: Bildad’s wicked man loses healing and security, a general parallel to Zophar’s doom of the ungodly.
job-11:20:9.why: Friends’ shared portrait of the wicked’s fate.

job-11:20:10.summary: Flight perishes from the runner and none saves his life, similar to deliverance abandoning them.
job-11:20:10.why: Image of failed escape in judgment.

job-11:20:11.summary: The rich man in Hades lifts his eyes in torment without relief, only loosely related to the wicked’s lost hope.

job-11:20:12.summary: Curse that “waste your eyes and melt away your life” echoes the eyes of the ungodly wasting away.
job-11:20:12.why: Ties the image to the covenant curses.

job-11:20:13.summary: The wicked flees in haste from God’s unsparing hand, loosely matching lost deliverance.
job-11:20:13.why: Similar portrait of the wicked’s flight.

job-11:20:15.summary: “What hope does the ungodly person have” directly matches the theme that the ungodly’s hope is destruction.
job-11:20:15.why: Job echoes Zophar’s point about the wicked’s hope.

job-11:20:16.summary: No one fleeing will escape God’s judgment, a general parallel to deliverance abandoning them.

job-11:20:17.summary: Fleeing a lion only to meet a bear pictures failed escape, loosely like abandoned deliverance.
